paper_metadata.title: Influence of alloying elements on mechanical and electronic properties of NbMoTaWX (X = Cr, Zr, V, Hf and Re) refractory high entropy alloys

evidence.quote: NbMoTaW refractory high entropy alloy (RHEA) has shown great potential applications for high temperature components due to its high temperature mechanical strength.

The phase structure, elastic properties, and electronic structure of alloyed NbMoTaWX (X = Cr, Zr, V, Hf and Re) RHEAs were predicted and the effect of alloying elements on the mechanical performance was investigated based on first-principle calculation and experiments.

Most of the alloying elements (X = Cr, Zr, V, Hf and Re) enhanced the strength of NbMoTaW RHEA, while only Zr-alloying improved both the strength and ductility simultaneously.
The formation of partial Zr – Zr metallic bonds effectively improved the strength and ductility of NbMoTaW RHEA from the perspective of experiments and theoretical predictions.

NbMoTaWX (X = Cr, Zr, V, Hf and Re) RHEAs ingots were produced by non-consumable arc melting under the protective Ar atmosphere. Small pieces of raw materials Nb, Mo, Ta, W, Cr, Zr, V and Hf with purity over 99.9 wt% were selected and used. All the raw materials were cleaned, polished, weighed in atomic ratio and placed in crucible orderly. Ar gas with high purity was injected when the vacuum degree in the furnace reached 2.5 × 10 3 Pa. All the ingots were repeatedly melted for five times in a water-cooled copper mold crucible in order to get homogeneous composition.

Ti alloying obviously enhanced both the strength (from 1058 MPa to 1343 MPa) and ductility (from 2.6% to 14.1%) of NbMoTaW RHEA [15].
The improvement of the ductility for Zr-alloying was attributed to the formation of Zr–Zr metallic bonds in the alloyed NbMoTaWX RHEAs.
The XPS results show that Zr – Zr metallic bonds were formed in NbMo - TaWZr alloy system, which well agreed with the theoretical prediction.

Besides, for all the alloyed RHEAs, W2 – Nb2, Nb2 – Ta2 and Nb1 – Mo2 bonds are less than zero, which means that these atoms no longer form the covalent bonds. They may relate to the metallic bonds. Therefore, the strength and ductility of these alloyed RHEAs were enhanced.
